messages:
maria: Hey folks — I have a customer ticket with request_id `8f3b7a2e` and a trace id `trace-0a1b2c3d`. Where's the fastest place to pull the logs + span view?
jack: For quick lookup I usually do Console -> Requests -> paste request id in search. Filters: time range = last 1h, service = inference.
ryan: If you prefer CLI: `redwoodctl logs find --request-id 8f3b7a2e` will return log lines + a link to the trace.
lisa: Note: if the request hit a fallback model the trace might be in the fallback pool — add `--pool fallback` or expand service filters.
maria: thanks — the console search didn't show anything, maybe outside time window. Is there a command to search broader?
jack: yep: `redwoodctl logs find --request-id 8f3b7a2e --since 24h` or set `--env prod` if multienv.
ryan: also check the trace UI: Console -> Traces -> paste `trace-0a1b2c3d`. If trace exists you'll get span waterfall + service tags and request_id annotation.
sre-bot: Incident hint: if logs are missing, check if request was sampled out. Sampling rate for traces is 1% by default; logs remain, but full spans may be dropped.
lisa: If you only have a trace id, you can map to request id by opening the trace and looking for `request_id` attribute on the root span or the inference-span.
maria: got the trace UI now, spans show `request_id: 8f3b7a2e` but logs are sparse — where do I fetch full request payload?
jack: Full payloads are stored in request-archive S3 (prod-archives). Use `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-archives/requests/2026/03/12/8f/8f3b7a2e.json -` — might need infra role.
ryan: shorter path: `redwoodctl payload get --request-id 8f3b7a2e` (uses internal role to fetch and prints JSON).
maria: tried `redwoodctl` and got permission denied. Is there a support workaround?
sre-bot: Ping @lisa — she can run with infra-read. Also open a quick access ticket with `#infra-requests` if this becomes frequent. :warning:
lisa: I pulled payload and pasted in the ticket. Also left a dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/req-search?request_id=8f3b7a2e
maria: perfect! One more Q: for future, any quick cheat sheet for others to follow?
jack: TL;DR: 1) Console Requests search -> request_id 
2) Console Traces -> trace id 
3) CLI `redwoodctl logs find` and `redwoodctl payload get` 
4) If not found, check S3 archive or sampling/retention windows
ryan: I'll add a short runbook to the observability wiki with commands and screenshots.
maria: thanks all — closing the loop here :white_check_mark:
